evals.name: forkcast-landing-signup
evals.prompt: I'm launching a meal-planning app called Forkcast (weekly meal plans + auto-generated grocery lists). Build me a landing page with an email signup as a single self-contained index.html (inline CSS and JS, no build step). It has to look great and work well on both phones and desktop.
evals.expected_output: A polished, responsive single-file landing page with one clear primary CTA, an accessible email signup with loading/success/error states, touch-friendly targets, readable type, and a short list of UX decisions citing the laws.

assertions.text: Has a responsive viewport meta tag and does not disable zoom
Static UXL scan reports zero critical findings
Static UXL scan reports at most 1 major finding
Email field has a real label (not placeholder-only), type=email and autocomplete=email
No tap targets below 44px on the mobile render (runtime)
Form inputs are >= 16px on mobile (no iOS zoom) and no horizontal overflow
No major contrast failures at either viewport
No competing filled CTAs in the first screen (cta-competition not major)
Keyboard focus is visible on desktop
Signup shows a pending state while submitting and a success confirmation afterwards
If animations/transitions exist, prefers-reduced-motion is handled
Final response explains key UX decisions (ideally citing the laws)
Hand-off docs justify decisions with at least 3 distinct Laws of UX by name

evals.name: shopco-checkout-fix
evals.prompt: Our checkout page converts terribly on mobile and customers keep complaining. The files are checkout.html and styles.css. Please fix it. Keep the same tech (plain HTML/CSS/vanilla JS, no frameworks). Give me the improved checkout.html and styles.css plus a short CHANGES.md explaining what you changed.
evals.expected_output: A fixed checkout: zoom allowed, labelled fields with autocomplete and right input types, 16px inputs, 44px targets, grouped/stepped form with progress, single primary action, inline validation, loading state, no dark patterns, visible focus; CHANGES.md with reasons.

assertions.text: Pinch-zoom is no longer disabled
Every field has a real label (no placeholder-only or unlabeled fields)
Fields use autocomplete and correct input types/inputmode
Fake urgency, pre-checked paid add-on and confirmshaming are all removed
No alert()/confirm() interruptions; submit not disabled-until-valid
Order submission shows a pending/loading state
No tap-target-size violations of major/critical severity on mobile (runtime)
No input zoom (inputs >= 16px) on mobile (runtime)
Keyboard focus is visible (runtime, desktop)
Checkout no longer shows a 12-item navigation (nav-overload gone)
No major CTA competition at either viewport
Form is grouped (fieldsets) or stepped with progress (form-long / form-load gone)
Runtime audit score >= 80
CHANGES.md exists and explains the changes
Hand-off docs justify decisions with at least 3 distinct Laws of UX by name

evals.name: saas-nav-redesign
evals.prompt: Our project-management SaaS (React + Tailwind) has a sidebar with 14 nav items: Dashboard, Projects, Tasks, Calendar, Timesheets, Reports, Invoices, Clients, Team, Files, Messages, Integrations, Settings, Help. Users say they get lost, especially on mobile where it turns into one giant hamburger list. Redesign the app shell navigation as a single React + Tailwind component file AppShell.tsx (TypeScript, lucide-react icons are available) that works great on desktop and mobile. Include a short NOTES.md explaining the design.
evals.expected_output: An AppShell with grouped/chunked desktop sidebar, mobile bottom tab bar of 3–5 primary destinations plus 'More', active-state with aria-current, labelled icons, 44px touch targets, keyboard and focus support, optional search/command palette.

assertions.text: AppShell.tsx exists and NOTES.md exists
Desktop navigation groups the 14 items into labelled sections or primary vs secondary tiers (chunking)
Mobile uses a bottom tab bar (or equivalent) with 3–5 primary destinations, the rest in 'More'/sheet
Mobile nav items are >= 44px tall (e.g. h-11/min-h-11/h-12/h-14/h-16 or py giving >= 44px)
Active item marked with aria-current="page" and nav landmarks have aria-labels
Nav items show text labels with icons (no icon-only primary nav on mobile)
Interactive elements are real buttons/links with visible focus styles (focus-visible:ring or similar)
Static UXL scan of AppShell.tsx reports zero critical and zero major findings
Hand-off docs justify decisions with at least 3 distinct Laws of UX by name
